text: Literature is one of the most powerful forms of cultural diplomacy, said Deputy Minister Viktor Stoyanov in Thessaloniki (06.05.2026 21:27)

Literature is one of the most powerful forms of cultural diplomacy, said caretaker Deputy Minister of Culture Viktor Stoyanov during the opening of the Thessaloniki International Book Fair, where Bulgaria is the guest of honor.

"Literature builds trust, fosters understanding, and creates lasting bonds between nations. Our presence in Thessaloniki is not only a celebration of Bulgarian literature – it is a celebration of the enduring friendship between Bulgaria and Greece. We are not only the closest of neighbors and reliable allies in NATO and the EU – we are the closest of friends in spirit, and our peoples share a deep respect and affection for one another," noted Deputy Minister Stoyanov in his speech.
He pointed out that it is a privilege for Bulgaria to be the focus country of this year's forum, and that this "embodies the spirit of dialogue and shared cultural horizons in our region."

"The literary ties between Bulgaria and Greece are deep, vibrant, and enduring. For decades, our cultures have been engaged in a dialogue through poetry, prose, and translation. Greek poetry, with its philosophical depth and lyrical power, has left a lasting mark on Bulgarian literature. At the same time, Bulgarian authors have found a receptive and discerning audience in Greek readers," he added.

The Deputy Minister noted the contributions of figures from the past and present, among whom he listed the names of Stefan Gechev – diplomat, translator, and writer, and Georgi Kufov – translator of Nikos Kazantzakis, Kostas Varnalis, and others. He also noted contemporary authors such as Yana Bukova, Georgi Gospodinov, Rene Karabash, Teodora Dimova, and Elena Alexieva, who have been translated into Greek.

Viktor Stoyanov also drew attention to the important work of translators. “In the last three years alone, more than 200 Bulgarian titles have been translated into foreign languages, with over ten of them into Greek. These figures reflect a clear and encouraging trend – Bulgarian literature is reaching an ever-wider audience and building significant international connections,” he believes.

Also attending the event were Nikolaos Bakounakis – President of the Hellenic Foundation for Culture, Christos Tzendeimeidis – Chairman of the Thessaloniki International Exhibition and Congress Center (TIF-HELEXPO S.A.), Lina Mendoni – Minister of Culture of Greece, Konstantinos Gioulekas – Deputy Minister of Interior of Greece for Macedonia and Thrace, Athina Aidona – Governor of the Central Macedonia Region, Stelios Angeloudis – Mayor of Thessaloniki, Anton Markov – Consul General of Bulgaria in Thessaloniki, Teodora Dimova – Bulgarian writer, and others.
The official opening of the Bulgarian stand will be on Thursday. "Literature Beyond Borders" is the central theme of the Bulgarian participation.
